fixes.explanation: Money doesn't come up in this verse, friend. The fight Paul names is quarreling over words. He says to charge the believers before God to avoid it. Take another look at the verse and you'll spot it, and I'll be right here cheering you on.

Ruin, baker. Paul says quarreling over words succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin (2 Timothy 2:14). Notice it's the listeners. They're the ones who end up hurt by all that arguing. That's why Paul charges the believers before God to avoid it.

Wisdom would be a nice surprise, friend, but that's not what Paul says. He says quarreling over words succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin (2 Timothy 2:14). Ruin is the word he uses for what it does to them. Good guess, though, and I'm glad you're thinking it through.
I'd love that outcome, baker. But unity isn't what Paul says here. He says quarreling over words succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin (2 Timothy 2:14). Ruin is the word to remember.

Not this time, baker. The workman Paul describes is an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth (2 Timothy 2:15). Temple records are a fine thing to keep tidy, but they're not what he names. I'd stamp a cookie with the word of truth any day before a filing cabinet.

Spread, baker. Paul says the talk of such men will spread like gangrene (2 Timothy 2:17). He's talking about the men he's just described, who speak irreverent, empty chatter. Their talk doesn't stay in one spot.

Close, friend, but this one is true. Paul says Hymenaeus and Philetus say that the resurrection has already occurred (2 Timothy 2:18). He also says they have deviated from the truth and undermine the faith of some. Tough one, and now you've got it for next time.

Wealth doesn't show up in this verse, baker. The seal says, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.” (2 Timothy 2:19) Iniquity is the thing to turn from. Keep that word handy.

That's the one, baker. Paul says to pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart (2 Timothy 2:22). Timothy isn't pictured chasing them alone. He's pictured alongside others who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

False, baker. Paul says a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing (2 Timothy 2:24). Quarrelsome is the one thing he rules out. I'd put that line up on my own bakery wall.

Gently, baker. Paul says the servant must gently reprove those who oppose him (2 Timothy 2:25). He says it's in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth. Think of pressing a cookie stamp. Gentle is the word Paul picks.
